summary: R233 extends R225 signature namespace isolation from source-log scope to source-log plus startup epoch. In an accumulated log containing multiple process startups, repeated runtime signature IDs and their declaration/compile/detail evidence no longer overwrite or merge across process epochs.

Read AGENTS.md, docs/reviews/VR_BACKEND_100_REVIEW_INDEX.md and Set05, docs/automation/QUEUE_CONTROLLER_CONTRACT.md, docs/CONVERSION_LANE_STATE.json, docs/VR_AUTODEV_STATE.json, docs/VR_RUN_STATE.md, docs/VR_REGRESSION_KNOWLEDGE.json and docs/VR_PROBLEM_HISTORY.md. C1_REVIEW.finding: R225 correctly scopes runtime signature IDs by source log, but accumulated logs can contain multiple process startups and runtime signature ordinals restart per process. Because SignatureKey is only (source_log, signature_id), startupA/signature#1 and startupB/signature#1 collide; setdefault preserves the older signature body while detail maps can be overwritten or merged by later epoch evidence.

review_lenses.adversarial: Single accumulated-log fixture repeats signature#1 across two startup epochs with distinct declaration and shader-compile evidence; both epochs must survive independently without cross-contamination.

C2_IMPLEMENT.evidence: SignatureKey now includes source_log, startup_epoch and signature_id. Each recognized startup advances the per-log epoch; legacy logs without a startup marker remain epoch 0. Signature report entries export startup_epoch and every declaration/FFP/texture/shader compile/prototype detail map uses the same epoch-scoped key. Added an accumulated-log repeated-signature regression and source-graph drift guards.
